content: Home Pakistan News Conservator Wildlife visits Ghazi, Tarbela, directs plantation in watershed areas Conservator Wildlife Visits Ghazi, Tarbela, Directs Plantation In Watershed Areas Published March 25, 2026 | 10:59 PM The Conservator Wildlife, Hazara Circle, paid an official visit to Ghazi and Tarbela, where he held a meeting with the Environment Department of the Tarbela Hydropower Project to review ongoing environmental and conservation initiatives TARBELA, (APP - UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 25th Mar, 2026) The Conservator Wildlife, Hazara Circle, paid an official visit to Ghazi and Tarbela, where he held a meeting with the Environment Department of the Tarbela Hydropower Project to review ongoing environmental and conservation initiatives. During the meeting, detailed discussions were held on ecological preservation and sustainable environmental practices in and around the project area. The Conservator emphasized the importance of restoring natural habitats and directed the concerned officials to ensure plantation of indigenous plant species in the watershed areas of Tarbela Dam. He noted that the use of native species would not only strengthen the local ecosystem but also help in soil conservation and biodiversity protection. Later, the conservator visited the Jhari Kass Wildlife Check Post, where he inspected the ongoing repair and maintenance work. Expressing dissatisfaction over the slow pace of progress, he issued strict instructions to the Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) and the concerned staff to accelerate the work. He further stressed that while expediting the completion process, maintaining quality standards should remain a top priority. The conservator warned that any negligence or unnecessary delays would not be tolerated and directed the field staff to ensure timely and efficient execution of all assigned tasks. The visit underscores the department’s commitment to environmental conservation, sustainable development, and effective monitoring of wildlife protection infrastructure across the Hazara region. content: Home Pakistan Water inflow rises at Tarbela Dam after recent rains Water Inflow Rises At Tarbela Dam After Recent Rains Published April 02, 2026 | 01:00 PM PESHAWAR, (APP - UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 2nd Apr, 2026) Recent rainfall in the upper districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has led to a noticeable increase in water inflow at Tarbela Dam, said the dam authorities on Thursday. Dam officials said that the water level in Tarbela Dam has risen to 1,451 feet, which is 49 feet above the dead level of 1,402 feet. The dam’s maximum level is 1,550 feet. The inflow of water into the dam has been recorded at 36,500 cusecs, while the outflow stands at 15,000 cusecs, indicating a steady accumulation of water due to the recent rains. Despite the improved water situation, power generation remains limited. Out of the dam’s 17 power generation units, only 4 units are currently operational, while 13 units are shut down. The total electricity generation capacity of Tarbela Dam is 4,988 megawatts, but currently, only 760 megawatts of electricity is being produced. Authorities have attributed the rising water levels to the recent rainfall in the upper regions of the province, which has positively impacted the reservoir levels. Further updates are expected as weather conditions evolve and water inflow continues to change, they said. content: Home Pakistan News Tarbela 5th Extension HPP advances towards carbon market registration Tarbela 5th Extension HPP Advances Towards Carbon Market Registration Published May 01, 2026 | 01:54 AM Tarbela 5th Extension Hydropower Project (T5) has achieved a significant milestone in WAPDA’s engagement with international carbon markets LAHORE, (APP - UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 30th Apr, 2026) Tarbela 5th Extension Hydropower Project (T5) has achieved a significant milestone in WAPDA’s engagement with international carbon markets. The Project is expected to reduce approximately 565,905 tons of CO2 emissions annually, contributing to a total reduction of 5,659,053 tons over a fixed 10-year crediting period, according to WAPDA spokesman here Thursday. The verification process for the Project has commenced and, upon completion, the Project will be registered with the Global Carbon Council (GCC). This will make T5 Pakistan’s first hydropower project to achieve GCC registration. The progress has been made possible with technical support from the World Bank and through the successful completion of key milestones, including project submission and the engagement of GCC-approved international verifier namely LGAI Technologies, Spain. As part of the verification process, a site visit was conducted by the local auditor of LGAI Technologies. During the visit, GM/PD T5, Umair Manan, briefed the auditor on the overall progress of the Project. Director (Civil) T5, Faisal Hayat, and Assistant Director Environment T5, Asima Mughal, also informed the auditor about ongoing construction activities, in addition to environmental and social management aspects of the Project. The auditor appreciated the progress achieved across various components of the Project and expressed satisfaction with compliance to environmental and social plans. The Tarbela 5th Extension Hydropower Project, on completion, will play a vital role in promoting clean energy and supporting Pakistan’s commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. The NDMA is maintaining close monitoring of reservoir levels and river flows and providing timely information and alerts to relevant authorities to strengthen preparedness against potential flooding. content: Home Pakistan River flows, flash flood risk rise across Pakistan: NDMA River Flows, Flash Flood Risk Rise Across Pakistan: NDMA Published August 08, 2026 | 08:30 PM ISLAMABAD, (APP - UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 8th Aug, 2026) The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) on Saturday warned of rising water flows in major rivers and the risk of low to moderate-level flooding across several parts of the country on August 8-9, as its National Emergencies Operation Centre (NEOC) reviewed river flows, reservoir levels and emerging monsoon risks and directed local administrations to pre-position resources and keep evacuation arrangements ready in vulnerable areas. According to the NEOC assessment, low-level flooding is currently being observed in the Indus River at Kalabagh, Chashma, Taunsa and Guddu. Flows in the Ravi, Chenab, Jhelum, Kabul and Sutlej rivers, as well as hill torrents in Dera Ghazi Khan and Rajanpur and Nullah Lai, remain normal. The NDMA said water flows in major rivers are expected to increase on August 8 and 9. Low-level flows are likely at Kalabagh, Chashma, Taunsa, Guddu and Sukkur on the Indus, Marala on the Chenab and Balloki on the Ravi. Low-level flows are also expected in the Jhelum and downstream areas of Mangla Dam, adjoining rivers and at Adezai on the Kabul River. The authority warned of low to moderate-level flooding in streams and nullahs in Chitral, Upper Dir, Abbottabad, Shangla, Khyber, Orakzai, Kohat, Tank and North and South Waziristan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. In Azad Kashmir, Bagh and Kotli face the risk of sudden low to moderate-level flooding, while similar risks have been identified in Zhob, Musakhel, Kohlu, Barkhan and Dera Bugti in Balochistan. In Punjab, hill torrents in Dera Ghazi Khan and Rajanpur could experience low to moderate flooding. Urban flooding is also possible in Rawalpindi, Gujranwala, Sialkot, Narowal, Faisalabad, Okara and Lahore.
